# Embedded-C++ skill

Idiomatic, safe C++ for embedded targets: modern subset (C++17), zero-cost
abstractions, deterministic resource management (RAII, no exceptions where
forbidden), template discipline, and MISRA C++:2023 conformance.

## 1. Purpose and scope

**Purpose.** Use C++ where its abstractions earn their keep — type-safe
drivers, compile-time configuration, testable interfaces — without paying in
unpredictability.

**In scope.** C++17 subset selection, RAII and deterministic lifetimes,
no-exception design, template/policy-based drivers, `constexpr` configuration,
static polymorphism (CRTP) vs virtuals policy, and C++-specific review checks.

**Non-goals.** Heap-heavy or RTTI/exception-based designs on constrained
targets; OS userspace C++ (follow `embedded-linux` plus standard practice).
Builds on `implementation` and `mcu`.

## 2. Normative sources (verified Phase 2, high confidence)

| # | Standard | Version / status | Clause / scope | Source |
|---|----------|------------------|----------------|--------|
| 1 | ISO C++17 | ISO/IEC 14882:2017 | Language baseline for safety-related embedded C++ | `https://www.iso.org/standard/68564.html` |
| 2 | MISRA C++ | MISRA C++:2023 (merged AUTOSAR C++14 rules, C++17) | Safety-related C++ subset | `https://misra.org.uk/` |
| 3 | AUTOSAR C++14 | R22-11 / R23-11 (superseded by MISRA C++:2023) | Historical basis; cite MISRA C++:2023 for new work | `https://www.autosar.org/standards/adaptive-platform/` |
| 4 | CERT C++ | Current | Secure-coding rules for C++ | `https://wiki.sei.cmu.edu/confluence/display/cplusplus/SEI+CERT+C%2B%2B+Coding+Standard` |

## 3. Subset rules

1. **C++17, bounded.** No exceptions on constrained targets (`-fno-exceptions`;
   error codes or `std::optional`/`expected`-style results); RTTI off
   (`-fno-rtti`) unless a documented use case survives review. Each relaxation
   is a project-level decision with a deviation record.
2. **RAII everywhere.** Resources (clocks, DMA channels, locks, handles) are
   owned by objects with deterministic destruction; manual acquire/release
   pairing outside constructors/destructors is a review finding.
3. **Templates with budgets.** Template drivers parameterized by policy;
   instantiation cost checked in the map file (code bloat is measured, not
   debated); recursive templates depth-bounded.
4. **Virtuals by policy.** Static polymorphism (CRTP/concepts-style) default on
   hot paths; virtual dispatch allowed where the vtable cost is budgeted and
   the hierarchy is closed (no unbounded external subclassing in safety paths).
5. **No heap after init** on constrained targets (same rule as C, `rtos` §5);
   containers are fixed-capacity (`std::array`, ring buffers) with
   bounds-checked access.

## 4. Construction patterns

1. **Drivers as policy classes.** Register access via typed register maps
   (`volatile` struct overlays reviewed once); bus behavior (I2C/SPI/UART) as
   policies so unit tests substitute loopback policies without hardware.
2. **`constexpr` configuration.** Clock trees, pin maps, and calibration tables
   computed at compile time where possible; `static_assert` guards invariants
   (buffer sizes, alignment, MPU granularity).
3. **Error taxonomy.** Project-wide `Status` enum (no bare `bool` for fallible
   ops); `[[nodiscard]]` on all status returns; error injection tested at the
   HAL seam.

## 5. Review checklist deltas

Exception/RTTI flags in build, implicit conversions, slicing, virtual-in-ctor,
static-init order across TUs, template bloat (map diff), `unsafe` missing —
no, that's Rust; instead: `reinterpret_cast` justification per use.

## 6. Verification of this skill (Phase 4 gate)

- C++17 + MISRA C++:2023 cited with version + URL (§2); AUTOSAR C++14 cited
  only as superseded basis.
- Build flags (`-fno-exceptions`, `-fno-rtti` where applicable) recorded and
  enforced in CI.
